name: Failed H&S / Rounded Top

card.context: A leader in an uptrend: above a rising 200-day (B26) and its 50-day on the trigger day, RS 80 or more (C31, pending), after a 25% advance. Best when the market itself is correcting and the stock refuses to break down. The short mirror lives below the 200-day (B26) and is the weakest-supported part of the card.
card.pattern: Three swing highs with the head 3% or more above the shoulders and a neckline through the lows (or a slow dome of 20 days or more), 15 to 100 days wide, 5% to 30% deep. The breakdown either never comes (A) or comes, falls under 10%, and is bought back (B).
card.trigger: OTHER: the first trade over the right-shoulder high (the dome high for a rounded top) after the failure, at market, no more than 4% past it.
card.stop: A few cents under the trigger day's low, within about 3%. The low of the failed breakdown is the invalidation line, not the stop: it sat a median 9.3% away.
card.failure_mode: The failure fails: price closes back under the neckline and the top works after all (Bulkowski's double bust), or the trigger whipsaws through a tight day-low stop before the real move (AAPL 2026). A late-stage top can be the last push (GOOGL 2026).

criteria.statement: The house meaning is the long: the breakdown everyone sees never comes, or comes and fails, and the squeeze fuels the next leg up. The classical neckline-break short is not a setup; the mirror short (a failed inverse H&S) is optional.

options.basis: long only, as the card and Bracco use it (the dossier's recommendation)
long plus the mirror short, a failed inverse H&S (8B), as an optional Red-market card
also the classical breakdown short (conflicts with B26 most of the time; -0.10R in the run)

criteria.evidence: Bracco 2026-04-19: 'Remember the only way to trade a H&S pattern is to trade the failure of it.' The Model Book card, the course plan (SET.29) and definitions.json all frame it long. Run: long B +0.11R (CI +0.07 to +0.16); the mirror short -0.02R below the 200-day; the neckline-break short -0.10R.

criteria.statement: An uptrend into the pattern: the close is above a rising 200-day SMA when the left shoulder forms, and the head is at least 25% above the lowest low of the 6 months before the left shoulder.

measure.what: head / lowest low of the 126 sessions before the left shoulder - 1
measure.and: close above a rising 200-day SMA at the left shoulder

criteria.evidence: Edwards and Magee item A ('a more or less extensive advance'), Murphy item 1 ('A prior uptrend'), StockCharts ('Without a prior uptrend ... there cannot be a Head and Shoulders reversal pattern'), Bulkowski ('Upward leading to the pattern'). The numbers are the dossier's; the app's detector has no trend test and fires in downtrends too. GOOGL 2026-09-18 passed the numbers while the real top was months earlier.

criteria.statement: H&S: three swing highs, each higher than the 5 bars on either side; the head at least 3% above the higher shoulder; the two shoulders within 10% of each other.

measure.and: |left shoulder - right shoulder| / higher shoulder <= 10%; each peak a 5-bar swing high

options.basis: the dossier's proposal

options.value: shoulders within 15%, 3-bar swings, no head minimum
options.basis: the app's head_shoulders.py

criteria.evidence: The shape is the originators' ('three peaks with the middle one highest'; Bulkowski: 'The two shoulders should peak near the same price'); the numbers are the dossier's. CAT 2024-07-18: shoulders 8.8% apart put the trigger almost at the head, stopped at once. The 10% is the outer limit, not the ideal; MSFT 2021's head only 1.4% over its shoulder was closer to a flat top.

criteria.statement: The neckline runs through the lowest lows between the peaks and slopes no more than 0.5% of price per day. If it sits above the buy point the pattern is mis-drawn: skip.
criteria.evidence: The slope limit is the app's too. DDOG 2025-01-28: the neckline ran 2.4% above the right-shoulder high at the trigger; the drawn pattern was not a top, the trigger failed in two days and the stock lost 40%.

criteria.statement: Rounded top: a slow arc of at least 20 trading days with no single swing high standing 3% above its neighbours; its neckline is the lower rim (the lowest low of the arc); the trigger is the dome high.

measure.and: no swing high 3% above its neighbours; the lower rim is the lowest low of the arc

options.basis: keep it in this setup, the dome high as the trigger (the dossier leans here; DECISIONS D-002's default)
split it into its own card
drop it: a close over a dome's high is a new-high breakout, close to the Flat Base and the Cup

criteria.evidence: Bulkowski's rim definition ('Downward breakouts are a close below the lower of the two rims'); his upward breakout from a rounding top ranks 2 of 39 (9% failure, 55% average rise). Run: 374 dome-high longs +0.03R, range crossing zero; the scan did not cover rounded tops. His own examples use it twice: the indexes in March 2026 ('Everyone obviously sees the big rounded top look') and AMD in August 2026.

criteria.statement: Left shoulder to right shoulder (or rim to rim) 15 to 100 trading days.

measure.what: sessions from the left shoulder to the right shoulder

criteria.evidence: IBD: 'as long as seven months to build'; Brandt: 'It is not unusual for H&S tops to be brief'. The ten examples ran 43 to 87 bars.

criteria.statement: Head to neckline 5% to 30%.
criteria.evidence: Bulkowski: 'Tall patterns perform better than short ones.' The run's median height 11.3% (middle half 7.7% to 16.0%); the examples 9.2% to 20.9%.

criteria.statement: Version B (preferred): at least one close under the neckline, or an intraday undercut of the right armpit low, that does not fall more than 10% under the neckline before the trigger.

measure.what: lowest close under the neckline before the trigger, as a share of the neckline
measure.and: at least one close under the neckline or an undercut of the right armpit low

options.basis: only after a neckline break (version B, Bracco's 'failed breakdown')
also when the break never comes (version A); the dossier recommends both with A graded lower (DECISIONS D-109's default)

criteria.evidence: Murphy: 'any decisive close back above the neckline is a serious warning that the initial breakdown was probably a bad signal'; Bulkowski's bust: 'drops no more than 10%, turns around'; Brandt's 'A' and 'B'. Bracco: 'the best way to trade a head and shoulders top is to buy the failed breakdown of it.' Run: +0.11R (+0.07 to +0.16) against +0.01R for the baseline; scan: 7,059 hits, 30.2% to 3R, 20.0% to 5R.

criteria.statement: Version A (allowed, graded lower): no close under the neckline; price turns up from the right shoulder.

measure.what: closes under the neckline before the trigger

criteria.evidence: The Model Book card's wording ('when the breakdown never comes'); Edwards and Magee's 'saved' patterns, 'perhaps 20%'. Run: +0.04R against +0.11R for version B; scan: 6,089 hits, 30.0% to 3R, no difference under a fixed stop. QQQ September 2025 (never closed under its August lows) is Bracco's version-A call.

criteria.statement: A brief, shallow undercut (under 6% below the neckline) is the A+ form; 6% to 10% grades lower.

measure.what: depth of the failed break under the neckline

criteria.dossier_ref: 9 A+; 4.5 depth of the failed break
criteria.evidence: Run: under 3% +0.12R; 3% to 6% +0.15R; 6% to 10% +0.05R (CI crosses zero). Six of the ten examples undercut 6% to 7% and still ran; the cue is a lean, not a gate.

criteria.statement: No hard volume rule. Trigger-day volume 1.25x or more of the 50-day average is a grading plus.
criteria.evidence: Bulkowski: 'Heavy breakout volume suggests better performance.' ICLR 2015-01-14 triggered on 1.0x and ran 25%; MGM 1.9x, MCO 2.6x.

criteria.statement: The close is above the 200-day SMA on the trigger day (hard).
criteria.evidence: 79% of version-B triggers in the run were above it, and all of the house's examples (SMH, QQQ, AMD). Above the 200-day only: +0.13R (+0.08 to +0.18).

criteria.statement: The close is above the 50-day SMA on the trigger day.
criteria.evidence: Bracco on SMH: 'Failed Head and Shoulders breakdown at $325. 50SMA the line in the sand to stay above.' And: 'Step 2 is remounting the 50SMA and the 20EMA.' SPG, BXP and TOL triggered with the stock back over the 50-day.

criteria.statement: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day on average.
The position is at most 1% of average daily volume.
RS rating 80 or more, in a top group.

measure.what: RS rating on the trigger day

options.basis: C31 as written (it is not a parabolic or mean-reversion trade)
a lower floor because the top itself pulled the RS down (the dossier's question)

criteria.evidence: A stock in a topping pattern has often lost relative strength by the time it fails. Patrick's AMD note led with 'Relative strength. Everyone saw rounding top and it gave nothing back'. The scan did not apply C31.

criteria.statement: The first trade above the right-shoulder high (the dome high for a rounded top) after the failure.

options.basis: the earlier close back over the neckline (Murphy's warning; a lower entry, less proof)
the right-shoulder high (Brandt's completion; the course plan; the dossier's recommendation)
a penny over the head (Bulkowski; the most proof, the highest entry)
a close through a falling line over the right side (Bracco's AMD, 2026-08-14)

criteria.evidence: Brandt: 'The advance today, May 18, penetrated the May 10 right shoulder high and officially completed the failure pattern.' The course plan already says 'entry over the right-shoulder high'. 75% of (b) triggers later traded over the head within 60 bars. AMD 2026: which peak counts as the right shoulder changed the outcome (the 08-04 high ran +3.9R, the 561.47 high ended at breakeven).

criteria.statement: For version B the trigger comes within 40 bars of the failure; the failure itself within 60 bars of the right shoulder.

measure.what: sessions from the failed break to the trigger
measure.and: the failure within 60 sessions of the right shoulder

criteria.evidence: The scan's windows. Run: the speed of the reclaim did not matter much (within 5 bars +0.10R; over 15 bars +0.13R).

criteria.statement: A market order once price is through the level, during regular hours.
criteria.evidence: E58 keeps it in regular hours. The scan bought at the level, or at the open when it gapped over.

criteria.statement: Not more than 4% above the right-shoulder high; on a gap past that, wait for a retest of the level or skip.

options.basis: keep C28 strict: skip or wait for a retest
allow a larger gap when the gap is the failure itself (SMH 2026-04-08 opened 4.6% over its right shoulder, his best example)

criteria.evidence: Many failures complete on a gap: SMH 2026-04-08 (+4.6%, then +7.4R), LULU 2023-03-29 (+11.4% after earnings, -1.0R), AMD 2026-09-22 (+8.0%, breakeven). C28 costs the house its best example; that is the question.

criteria.statement: At entry, no more than 10% above the 10-day average.
criteria.evidence: Run: the C28 and C29 filters together left +0.13R (+0.06 to +0.19) on 3,482 trades.

criteria.statement: No new buy in the 3 sessions before a report.
criteria.evidence: Several failures complete on earnings gaps (LULU 2023, TWLO 2026); FDX 2003, MCO 2011 and NFLX 2025 triggered on reaction days, after the report, so B22 allowed them.

criteria.statement: A few cents under the trigger day's low, with a real stop order.

measure.value: a few cents under the trigger day's low

options.basis: a few cents under the trigger day's low (the house default; Brandt's own line; the dossier's recommendation)
under the low of the failed break (a median 9.3% away, only 4% within 3%)

criteria.evidence: Brandt: 'The market should probably not take out Wednesday's low', the trigger day. The owner: 'Stop at LOD if this triggers. My stops are always LOD until I can raise them to breakeven'. Run: median 2.1%, within 3% for 68%; the examples 1.1% to 2.7%. The scan used 5 cents under the lower of the trigger day's and prior day's lows.

criteria.statement: If the stop is more than about 3% under the entry, size it down to the risk or skip.
criteria.evidence: Run by stop width: 2% or less +0.11R (win 28%); 2% to 3% +0.07R; over 3% +0.15R (win 41%). AAPL 2026-08-28: a 1.5% stop under a big stock's trigger day was tight; stopped the next session, then the stock ran to 350.

criteria.statement: The low of the failed breakdown is the invalidation line, not the stop.

measure.what: stop placed at the failed-break low

criteria.evidence: A stop under the failed-break low was a median 9.3% away (4% within 3%). SPG 2005: the invalidation line (61.03) sat far from the usable 1.1% stop.

criteria.statement: A real stop order with the broker. It only moves up.
A gap through the stop: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if that is past 2R.

measure.what: loss at the first 30-minute low of the gap-down day

criteria.statement: Stop to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.

measure.what: R at which the stop moves to the entry

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 3R.
criteria.evidence: Among the ten examples 3R came in 1 to 21 days (FDX, MCO and MUSA in a day; ICLR in 21).

criteria.statement: Sell a third at 5R.
If it opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
Trail the last third: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, under the 21-day for a steadier one.
criteria.evidence: Nothing in the sources argues for a different trail. ICLR's slow three weeks to 3R, then a 25% run, is the case for the trail.

criteria.statement: Time stop: still under 1R after 10 trading days, sell.
A reference, not a rule: the head is the first place sellers may return; Brandt's target is the right-shoulder high plus the distance from the head down to the post-break low.
criteria.evidence: Brandt: 'The target of 733 is based on projecting the distance between the April 26 high and the May 12 low (which is 69 cents) upward from the right shoulder high of 664.' After the failures that cleared the head, the median best high within 60 bars was 9.0% over the head.

criteria.statement: Count the tries: at most 3 in a week and 6 in a month. Failures whipsaw; a second entry over the same level is allowed.
criteria.evidence: Bulkowski: of busted H&S tops 67% single bust, 3% double, 30% triple or more, so almost a third of busts whipsaw before the final move. AAPL 2026-08-28: stopped the next session, then the run to 350 without the trade.

criteria.statement: Before the trigger: a fall of more than 10% under the neckline. The top worked; this setup is gone.

measure.what: lowest close under the neckline, as a share of the neckline

criteria.evidence: Bulkowski's bust rule: 'moves less than 10% away from the breakout price'. Run: 36% of neckline breaks fell 10% or more first.

criteria.statement: Before the trigger: a close under the 200-day.
After the buy: a close back under the neckline is a failure of the failure; the stop should already be above that.
criteria.evidence: Bulkowski's double bust. The stop under the trigger day's low usually sits above the neckline already.

criteria.statement: A Green or Yellow reading (F65); in Orange, A+ only.
criteria.evidence: The run's edge was largest with SPY under its 50-day (+0.30R, win 37%, against +0.02R above it), a correction, which F65 sizes down rather than forbids; the reading decides size, the correction supplies the edge.

criteria.statement: A cue: best when the market itself is correcting or just turning up and the stock's top fails anyway, the leader refusing to break while the market falls.
criteria.evidence: Bracco: 'this is why coming out of corrections I try to get a position in TQQQ and SOXL'; his March and April 2026 index calls. Run: SPY under its 50-day +0.30R (+0.21 to +0.38). MUSA 2022-03-15 (the early-2022 correction) and FDX 2003-03-19 (the 2003 low) are the examples.

criteria.statement: The index version: read the pattern on the index ETF (QQQ, SMH); trade the leveraged ETF if desired (E54).
criteria.evidence: Bracco: 'My main trading vehicle is always the TQQQ, SOXL, or Index futures.' SMH 2026-04-08 (+7.4R) and QQQ 2026-04-08 (+9.9R) are the house's own calls.

measure.what: the chart the pattern is read on
measure.value: the index ETF (QQQ, SMH); the order may go in the leveraged ETF

criteria.statement: Grade it lower when the stock has already run for a year or more: a failed top late in a long advance can be the last push.
criteria.evidence: Edwards and Magee: 'A Head-and-Shoulders Formation that does not work is a warning that even though there is still some life in the situation, a genuine turn is near.' GOOGL 2026-09-18: a lower-high structure under a higher May high; 0.8R, then down 20%.

criteria.statement: Never short the right shoulder before the neckline breaks, and the neckline break is not taught as a short setup: 70% of breaks from tops above the 200-day happen above it (B26), and the run lost -0.10R.

measure.what: neckline breaks from tops above the 200-day that were still above it on the break day

criteria.evidence: Murphy: the topping signs are cause 'to liquidate long positions, but not necessarily enough to justify new short sales.' The app's own short stop (1% over the right shoulder) was a median 9.6% away. The course can teach the break as a sell signal for a long and as the event that sets up the failure.

criteria.statement: Keep the name 'Failed H&S / Rounded Top' (Brandt's 'H&S failure' and Bulkowski's 'Busted Top' are the outside names).
criteria.evidence: DECISIONS D-016's default keeps the house name. No one coined the two halves as one setup; the only UCT use of both together is Bracco's 'failed rounded top / H&S' (AMD, 2026-08-16).

a_plus: fh.leadership: a leader, RS 80 or more, a top group, a big prior advance (fh.prior_trend; the AMD and SMH examples)
fh.hs_structure: a clear, widely visible top, the head 3% or more above both shoulders, or an obvious dome (fh.rounded_top); a level or rising neckline (fh.neckline)
fh.failure_b: version B with a brief, shallow undercut under 6% that is bought back (fh.undercut_depth_cue)
fh.trigger: the trigger over the right-shoulder high on rising volume (fh.volume_cue), within 4% of the level (fh.no_chase), with a stop of 3% or less (fh.stop_width)
fh.above_200: above a rising 50-day and 200-day on the trigger day (fh.above_50)
fh.market_correcting_cue: the market correcting or just turning up, the index itself failing to break down
fh.earnings: no report in the next 3 days
b_minus: fh.failure_a: version A with no undercut, or an undercut 6% to 10% deep that recovers slowly (fh.undercut_depth_cue)
fh.leadership: a stock that was not a leader; fh.late_stage: a year or more into its advance
fh.no_chase: a gap trigger more than 4% over the level (skip; B- at best if bought on a retest)
fh.hs_structure: a messy structure, the head barely above a shoulder (MSFT 2021, 1.4%), or a 'rounded top' that is really a range
fh.retries: the second or third try on the same pattern
no_trade: fh.inv_deep_break: a fall of more than 10% under the neckline, the top worked
fh.neckline: the neckline sits above the buy point, a mis-drawn pattern
fh.no_chase: more than 4% past the right-shoulder high; fh.not_stretched: more than 10% over the 10-day
fh.stop_width: the honest stop does not fit; fh.invalidation_line: never the failed-break low as the stop
fh.not_a_short: shorting the right shoulder or the neckline break

lookalikes.tell: Count the peaks and find the trigger. A 2B breaks one prior swing low and is bought the moment price reclaims that low, within 1 to 3 sessions, with the stop under the new low. A failed H&S has three peaks over a neckline and waits for the trade over the right-shoulder high, with the stop under that day's low.

Look at the ceiling. A flat base holds one range 15% deep or less with a flat top tapped twice and breaks out over it; a rounded top is a dome that first broke its lower rim (or sagged toward it) and then recovered, so the buy over the dome high comes after a failure, not out of a box.

Ask when the buy comes. A mean-reversion long buys the turn on the flush day itself, into a level, and is out in 1 to 5 sessions at the average; a failed H&S waits weeks for the undercut to be bought back and then for the trade over the right-shoulder high, and holds for a trend.

invalidations: Before the trigger: a fall of more than 10% under the neckline; the top worked (fh.inv_deep_break).
Before the trigger: a close under the 200-day (fh.inv_200).
Before the trigger: the neckline sits above the right-shoulder high; the pattern is mis-drawn (fh.neckline).
Before the trigger: no trigger within 40 bars of the failure (fh.trigger_window).
Before the trigger: a report within 3 sessions, wait (fh.earnings).
After the buy: the stop is the exit (fh.stop_broker); a close back under the neckline is a failure of the failure (fh.inv_after_buy).
After the buy: under 1R after 10 trading days, sell (fh.time_stop).
mistakes: Shorting the right shoulder before the neckline breaks. Murphy: the topping signs are cause 'to liquidate long positions, but not necessarily enough to justify new short sales.'
Calling every three bumps a head-and-shoulders. Brandt: 'novice market analysts are way to quick to mislabel market action as a H&S configuration.'
Buying the first bounce back to the neckline. That is the return move the short sellers expect; wait for the right-shoulder high.
Using the undercut low as the stop. It is usually far more than 3% away.
Chasing a gap far over the right shoulder (LULU 2023, 11.4%).
Trading it below the 200-day, or in a laggard whose 'top' was never a top.
Forgetting Edwards and Magee's warning: a failed top late in a long advance can be the last push (GOOGL 2026).
Re-buying every whipsaw. Count the tries (E56).
Drawing the neckline above the buy point (DDOG 2025): a mis-drawn pattern is not a top at all.
Reading the app's detector text as sourced: its Brandt quote, its Bulkowski '60-70%' and its 'Wyckoff 1908' are not in the sources.

short_mirror.note: 8B, a failed inverse head-and-shoulders (Bulkowski's busted H&S bottom): a stock below a falling 200-day (B26), RS 20 or less (C31 mirror), forms three swing lows with the middle lowest, closes over its neckline, rises less than 10%, and comes back; short the first trade under the right-shoulder low (Brandt's 'C' mirrored; Bulkowski a penny under the head), stop a few cents over the trigger day's high within about 3%, thirds at 3R and 5R, trail the rest on a close above the 10-day; skip if hard to borrow (D48); a Red market is its best condition (D46). Evidence: Bulkowski, 16% of H&S bottoms bust and single busts drop 22% on average; the run found -0.01R below the 200-day (CI -0.06 to +0.05), better than the baseline short (-0.08R) but not positive. The weakest-supported part of the dossier; whether to teach it is D-001. The classical neckline-break short is not proposed (8C).

best_conditions: A Green or Yellow reading (F65); in Orange, A+ only. The edge was largest when the market itself was correcting (SPY under its 50-day, +0.30R) and a leader's top failed anyway: Bracco's 'coming out of corrections' and his March and April 2026 index calls. For the index version read the pattern on QQQ or SMH and trade TQQQ or SOXL if desired (E54, pending D-018).

management.trail: a close under the 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one (E52)
management.breakeven: between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default (B19)
management.gap_open: a trim level the day opens past is taken at the open (F63)
management.gap_against: the first 30-minute low is the new stop; out if past 2R (B20)
management.retries: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month (E56); failures whipsaw
management.overrides: none. The dossier (8A) finds nothing in the sources that argues for different trims. References only: the head as the first place sellers may return, and Brandt's measured target (the right-shoulder high plus the head-to-post-break-low distance). Not ours: the app's H&S narrative 'cover part at 1R for a free trade', its short levels, and the rounded-top detector's stop (never within 3%).

base_rate.window: 60 bars forward, fixed stop 5 cents under the lower of the trigger day's and prior day's lows (the trigger day's low alone past 3%, skipped past 5%), no trims, no breakeven, no trail; 2000-01-01 to 2026-11-09 on all 2,630 liquid names; H&S only (no rounded-top scan); no grading, no market filter, no RS filter

house_run_2010_2026_600_tickers.note: the app's own detectors run every 5th bar, house management, survivors only, no costs; the writer's scripts were read, not re-run, in the cold check

failures.why: a clean 51-bar pattern (shoulders 317.40 / 320.28, head 13.5% over the neckline, a 2.8% undercut); the trigger over 320.28 was stopped the next session (stop 315.40, 1.5% away, best 0.0R), then the stock ran to 350 without the trade. A whipsaw, not a wrong read: count the tries and allow a second entry over the same level.

the shoulders were 8.8% apart (334.87 left, 364.43 right), so the right-shoulder high sat almost at the head and the trigger was late and high; stopped at once (best 0.0R), two months of chop before the autumn run. Uneven shoulders grade lower; the 10% tolerance is the outer limit.

the neckline sloped up so steeply that it ran 2.4% above the right-shoulder high at the trigger: the drawn pattern was not a top. Failed in two days (best 0.0R); the stock lost 40% after its February earnings.

the H&S formed under a higher May high (405), a lower-high structure in a stock that had already topped; the trigger at 351.60 stalled under the 50-day and the neckline, reached 0.8R, and the stock fell 20% by late October. Edwards and Magee's 'last push' warning.

Bracco's autumn 2025 call: the failed breakdown at $325 under the $333 neckline; under the right-shoulder trigger (360.00, the dossier's reading of his chart) it stopped out on 2025-12-12 (-1.0R), and SMH later rose past 400. Which level is the right shoulder, and the stop, decided the outcome.
the failure completed on an earnings gap 11.4% over the right shoulder (C28 says skip); bought anyway, -1.0R.

a 67-bar pattern (shoulders 110.64 / 107.58, head 19.1% over the neckline, a 2.0% undercut), buy 107.59, stop 104.59 (2.8%); the next session opened at 96.73, under the stop, and the stock lost 20.1% within 60 sessions: the top worked, and the first 30-minute low with the 2R cap is the exit.

examples.limits: The scan is the H&S half of 8A only; no rounded-top scan was written. The stop, chase and stretch rules are house defaults with no discretion; the market reading, the RS rating and the grading were not applied, so the base rate is a floor for an ungraded signal. The earnings table was used only to flag trigger days. The house run's R results were read from the writer's summary files, not re-executed. Survivors only; no costs.

near_misses.why: the head is 4.7% over the neckline (rule: 5% to 30%): a flat shelf in an uptrend, not a top; an ETF; stopped at 0R.
shoulders 226.75 / 254.67, 11.0% apart (rule: within 10%): a V recovery with the right shoulder near the head, a late and high trigger; stopped at 0R.
a close 10.9% under the neckline before the trigger (rule: more than 10% and the top worked): a completed top and a V recovery; stopped at 0R.
the trigger close is 2.6% under the 200-day SMA (rule: above it, B26): a bounce inside a decline; stopped at 0R.

question_seeds.seed: Where is the buy on a failed head-and-shoulders: the neckline, the right-shoulder high, or the head?
What is the low of the failed breakdown used for, and why is it not the stop?
The house trades the failed H&S in which direction, and what does Bracco say is the only way to trade the pattern?
Hidden ticker: tap the two lows the neckline runs through, then the right-shoulder high.
Hidden ticker: which of these four tops broke its neckline, fell less than 10%, and was bought back?
Hidden ticker: is this failed top above a rising 200-day with the stock back over its 50-day? Take it or pass.
Failed H&S or 2B: price undercut a prior low and reclaimed it in two days. Is the buy now, or over the right-shoulder high?
